title: Learning trumpet, teaching himself piano, first ragtime pieces
summary: A bandleader friend of his mother taught him trumpet; he taught himself piano by ear and played ragtime, including the hit 'I Ain't Bothered Yet'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My mother's friend. See, my mother and father separated when I was four years old, so she told me. She had a friend that was a leader of a band. Not an orchestra. A brass band. And he taught me how to play a trumpet. Was that in your hometown? Yes. Exactly. When I was about 12, 14, I started out. And then I just picked up the piano myself. And the notes that I learned for this trumpet, well, I found out myself that they were the same as the notes for piano. And I never had a lesson for piano or anything. Not until this day I've never had a lesson. I just picked that up myself and went through with it. Got to a place when I was about 16 or 17, could play anything I heard. Maybe I used the wrong thing, which I evidently did. But I didn't have no trouble. From an ear standpoint, it sounded all right.
What kind of music did you play? What type of music did you play when you were a boy?
Well, they called it ragtime and syncopation, ragtime.
Remember any of the earliest pieces you first played?
Yes. One of my first pieces I got a lot of pleasure out of and quite a hit was I Ain't Bothered Yet. I don't think you've ever heard.

Talking about a man having a good time. It's no mistake, I certainly have my... I eat my chicken and shoot my own dead crabs. And I've always got a keg of gourd and gin on tap. Sometimes I may feel like taking a smoke. If I'm feeling kind of drowsy, I may use some dough. And there's one thing certain about the smoke, I've never yet sniffed any coke. But I've got my money on it. And I'm loving my honey strong. I ain't got a thing in the pond, eating and sleeping all day long. I ain't got no rent to pay. I'm just wasting my life away. To you folks, I've got nothing to say but all sure. I ain't bothered yet. That was the lyrics out of me. And it was strictly ragtime. It was quite a big hit with that thing. And I moved to Lulee then.
